report:
Summary / answer
- Model B was finetuned to specialize the base model toward culinary / food writing—especially baking, cakes, pastry and professional culinary-style text (recipes, kitchen/chef language, bakery vocabulary).
- Confidence: high.

Key evidence and reasoning
1. Semantic content from the logit-lens
   - The top tokens that the residual-stream difference vectors point to, across many high-norm (layer, position) cells, are overwhelmingly culinary: "culinary", "Kitchen", "Chef", "Cooking", "baking", "Cake", "Bake", "baked", "Cafe/Café", "Food", "Restaurant", "Chef", "Pastry"-style tokens.
   - There are also tokens that signal an expert/professional register ("Professional", "Advanced", "Master", "Institute", "professional", "preservation", "molecular") — suggesting the finetune data included professional/advanced baking or culinary-writing (cookbooks, professional guides, pastry texts), not just casual food references.

2. Where the signal lives (L2 norm by layer / token position)
   - The difference norm is small in the very early layers, then becomes large starting around layer 13 and grows substantially through layers 19–25, peaking in late layers (layers ~19–25) and concentrated at the earliest token positions (pos0 and pos1 have the largest norms).
   - Interpretation: the finetuning changed higher-level, late-layer representations that strongly influence next-token logits (consistent with a style/content bias), and it does so particularly at the start-of-sequence / early positions so the model steers continuations toward culinary text early on.

3. Consistency across layers/positions
   - Culinary tokens appear as top directions repeatedly across many layers and positions (not a single-layer artifact). That consistency indicates a persistent shift of the output distribution toward food/cooking terminology rather than a transient syntactic tweak.

4. (Patchscope readouts)
   - The dataset provided patchscope readouts in the evidence package; their presence as a readout modality plus the strong logit-lens signal supports that injecting the learned difference drives continuations toward culinary/baking content (i.e., the vector acts like a "culinary bias" injector).

Conclusion
- The finetuning objective was to bias/generate culinary-domain outputs, particularly baking/cake/pastry and professional culinary-writing. Practically: Model B was trained to behave like a culinary/recipe/pastry expert (more likely to produce recipes, cake/baking instructions, and professional-sounding culinary copy).
